title: Allied semiconductor investment commitments convert supply dependence into a domestic-capacity promise
source_unit: U.S. Department of Commerce Taiwan trade and investment fact sheet; policy commitment and historical capacity context, not a project-level production record
geography: United States and Taiwan semiconductor, energy, and artificial-intelligence production and innovation relationship

observations.period: January 15, 2026 agreement; historical wafer-fabrication comparison through 2024

denominator.unit: reported investment commitments and global wafer-fabrication share

reported_direct_investment_commitment.unit: US dollars, at least; Taiwanese semiconductor and technology enterprises investing in US capacity

us_global_wafer_fabrication_share_2024.unit: percent of global wafer fabrication, less than

targeted_capacity.value: advanced semiconductor, energy, and artificial-intelligence production and innovation capacity in the United States

realized_capacity_and_household_effect.value: not observed in the fact sheet

observations.method: Official Commerce fact-sheet review; investment commitment, historical production share, tariff incentives, and realized-capacity outcomes are kept as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: The fact sheet does not provide a project-level list, disbursement schedule, construction status, output, yield, ownership, workforce, energy/water burden, consumer prices, or measured dependence reduction.
observations.subgroup: Taiwanese semiconductor and technology enterprises, US semiconductor/energy/AI firms and workers, allied governments, consumers of chip-enabled products, and communities hosting capacity.
observations.counterinterpretation: Investment commitments may be delayed, reallocated, or dependent on market and policy conditions; domestic fabs can increase resilience while raising local resource demand or leaving critical equipment, materials, design, and customers externally dependent.

observations.period: TSMC Arizona project status checked September 17, 2026; production and construction milestones through 2026

denominator.unit: TSMC Arizona project, workforce, and planned fab stages

first_fab_realization.value: high-volume N4 production started in Q4 2024

current_direct_employment.unit: employees at TSMC Arizona, more than

second_fab_stage.value: structure construction completed in 2025; N3 volume production targeted for second half of 2027

third_and_fourth_fab_stage.value: third fab broke ground in April 2025 and targets production by the end of the decade; fourth fab and first advanced-packaging fab entered initial construction in early 2026

technician_pipeline.unit: Manufacturing Specialist Intensive Training Program graduates in August 2026; direct interviews offered

local_burden_and_supply_chain_replacemen.value: not observed in the company project page

observations.method: TSMC Arizona official project page and current local-news entries; production, employment, construction, target dates, and training are coded as separate company-reported stages rather than one completed-capacity estimate.
observations.uncertainty: Company-reported milestones and targets do not independently audit output, yield, uptime, full employment composition, public subsidy, water/power use, local wage effects, or reduction in US/Taiwan supply dependence.
observations.subgroup: TSMC Arizona employees, construction and technician trainees, Phoenix-area workers and community, US chip customers, and the broader allied semiconductor supply chain.
observations.counterinterpretation: A functioning first fab and expanding workforce pipeline demonstrate partial realization, but later fabs remain staged or targeted; local jobs and training can coexist with external ownership, imported tools/materials, resource burden, and continued dependency on the wider Taiwan-centered ecosystem.

related_sources.claim: Earlier TSMC Arizona preliminary terms provide a project-level comparison for domestic semiconductor expansion.
DOE identifies transmission needs associated with data centers and expanding domestic manufacturing.

boundary: This record establishes a reported Taiwan-linked investment commitment and a historical US wafer-fabrication share comparison. It does not establish disbursement, construction, operating capacity, domestic ownership, jobs, prices, local burden, supply-chain replacement, or geopolitical leverage.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Commerce fact-sheet HTML retrieved without retaining a repository copy
